key_insight: A symmetry-based single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the low-energy band structure, spin splitting, and spin polarization of chiral 1D (R/S-PEA)PbI3 with only a small number of spin-dependent hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This gives a compact, interpretable electronic model for designing and screening chiral perovskites with targeted optical, spintronic, and transport properties.
method: Built a single effective orbital on each of four symmetry-related sites in the primitive cell.
Included layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate parameter sets for conduction and valence bands.
Analyzed degeneracies using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary symmetries to distinguish symmetry-enforced from accidental crossings.
evidence_signal: The model was benchmarked against density-functional-theory band structures and shown to quantitatively capture band-edge spin splittings and leading Bloch-state spin-polarization patterns.
watch_item: Because the model uses fitted conduction/valence parameters and only a restricted set of hopping terms, it may miss effects beyond the low-energy window or in perturbed structures.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
